caveats: 58 of 280 tests have an "end of test" label that disagrees with the recorded extinction diameter; the label is used (decision D22).
Methanol and heptane droplets in one apparatus: this is one experiment family, not independent confirmation.
Tests were not designed as a controlled sweep of oxygen alone: pressure and diluent also vary.
sentences: At oxygen fractions below 0.16, 45 of 48 FLEX droplet tests (94%) ended in extinction; at 0.24 or above, 9 of 49 (18%) did.

The other end states in the report are "completion" (the droplet burned to completion) and "disruption" (a disruption ended the test); both are counted as "not extinguished" here and are listed in the table.
With carbon dioxide in the diluent: 88 of 123 tests ended in extinction (72%).
With helium in the diluent: 45 of 56 tests ended in extinction (80%).
With nitrogen only: 58 of 101 tests ended in extinction (57%).
items.title: FLEX droplets: oxygen and diluent versus extinction

caveats: Highest oxygen in the table: 0.85 (matches the official text: up to 85% oxygen from a spherical burner).
Fuel (ethane, propane, butane and mixtures), pressure and flow also vary between tests.
Outcome classes follow the PSI label (self-extinguished or flow terminated) plus comment rules (OUTCOME_MAPPING.md).
sentences: Oxygen 0 to 0.21: 29 tests; 15 self-extinguished, 5 stopped by the operator or flow cut-off while still burning, 2 did not ignite.
Oxygen 0.21 to 0.3: 74 tests; 31 self-extinguished, 12 stopped by the operator or flow cut-off while still burning, 30 did not ignite.
Oxygen 0.3 to 0.4: 124 tests; 59 self-extinguished, 39 stopped by the operator or flow cut-off while still burning, 23 did not ignite.
Oxygen 0.4 to 1.01: 106 tests; 68 self-extinguished, 35 stopped by the operator or flow cut-off while still burning, 1 did not ignite.
"Stopped while still burning" is a censored outcome: the flame had not gone out when the test ended, so it is not counted as an extinction.

strength_rule:
(deterministic, see docs/RANKING.md section 3):
  moderate  = at least 100 tests in one experiment family (never 'strong': strong would need two independent families agreeing)
  limited   = 30 to 99 tests
  very limited = fewer than 30 tests
A source conflict that touches the analysis lowers the label by one step; a high share of unknown outcomes is stated beside it.
